source.title: Noise as a Resource for Learning in Knowledge Distillation
source.authors: E. Arani; Fahad Sarfraz; Bahram Zonooz

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendix tables, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies the fraction of corrupted training labels and measures test accuracy, but does not report training error on those conditions.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy for knowledge distillation and Messy Collaboration at several label-corruption and target-noise rates. Rows below extract vanilla knowledge distillation (target-noise rate r=0) across corruption rates; its remaining results are not needed to represent the version tested. The cited Arpit et al. result is prior work, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates knowledge distillation and a proposed memorization regularizer using test accuracy. It reports no training accuracy, training loss, or direct memorization measure. Decreasing test accuracy under label corruption cannot establish V4's perfect training fit or memorization of noise. Memorization motivates the method but is not itself measured.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that knowledge distillation improves generalization under noisy labels and that Messy Collaboration often improves it further. They interpret these gains as suggesting that target variability discourages memorization; they do not directly measure reduced memorization.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains WRN students by knowledge distillation on CIFAR-10 or SVHN with corrupted labels; it does not reproduce the original random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and label-corruption rate change test accuracy; the tested corruption rates are discrete.

fits_no_version.finding: With vanilla distillation, test accuracy decreases monotonically over the reported corruption rates: 94.26% to 67.97% on CIFAR-10 and 96.81% to 91.93% on SVHN. Training fit is unreported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Knowledge-distilled WRN-16-2 students generalize progressively worse as training-label corruption increases from 0% to 50% on CIFAR-10 and SVHN.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Workshop/Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
record.problems: The study reports generalization accuracy but no training error, so it cannot establish whether the models fit the corrupted training labels perfectly. The tested corruption rates are discrete rather than a continuous sweep.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported results vary Messy Collaboration target-noise rates and include baseline, teacher, and CINIC accuracy; omitted because the extracted vanilla-distillation rows already show the tested version's test-accuracy trend. See Tables 7–9 and Figures 4–5.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random training labels, chance test performance, and preservation of architecture and training hyperparameters.
Training time and convergence speed for true versus random labels, including dependence on corruption fraction.
Zero training error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Additive Gaussian augmentation is a different experiment.

Perfect training fit while test error degrades toward chance across increasing random-label corruption. Only test performance at corruption rates from 0 to 0.50 is reported; neither perfect fit nor noise memorization is established.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting and whether removing it harms true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels; no relevant training trajectories or learning-order measurements are reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reported test-accuracy trend agrees with one component of V4, but the mitigation-only exclusion applies because the study never measures fitting or memorizing corrupted labels. Missing training-fit measurements are untested parts, not omitted results. Other performance comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment fits completely random labels and reports training error or test error at chance.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed for true versus random labels.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input fitting experiment.
Training-set fit or training error is not reported. The study evaluates selected label-corruption rates, not a continuous sweep from none to all.
No test of whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation prevent fitting random labels, or whether removing them changes true-label generalization.
No analysis of learning order or comparison of when real versus random labels are learned.

relation.reason: Section 4.3 discusses memorization as motivation and interprets generalization gains as discouraging it, without directly testing the cataloged effects.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates generalization under noisy labels and a proposed mitigation, without measuring training fit, memorization, or learning order. Its results do not test a claim version.

source_check.notes: All twelve student values and their standard deviations match Tables 7–8. Corruption reaches 0.50; no training-fit or direct memorization measure establishes V1–V6.
